results.label: a direct `eval` still reads the same names: renaming is switched off for the whole file (and the report says so)
with `eval` present nothing is renamed and nothing is removed, and the report names the hazard that blocked renaming
inside a `with` block the name `undefined` is NOT re-spelled as `void 0` — it may be a property of the object, and the trap is measured
the printed `with` body still says `undefined` (a `void 0` there would have returned nothing instead of the property)
a binding read or written inside a `with` body keeps its name: the lookup is by name at run time
the report says the binding was left alone because a `with` block makes the name dynamic
the `Function` constructor also switches renaming off
a name that appears inside a string is never reused as a different name
the binding whose name appears in a string keeps that name, and the report says why
with nothing in the way, short names are handed out (renaming is not simply disabled everywhere)
an anonymous function assigned to a binding keeps the binding name, so `fn.name` is unchanged
the report lists that binding as skipped with the reason (it is not silently renamed)
arity is not touched: `fn.length` and `arguments.length` are the same before and after
no parameter was dropped from the printed signature
property names are never mangled: `.name`, `["name"]` and the key in an object literal all survive
a property read whose value is unused is still performed (a getter is not a no-op)
the read survives as its own statement rather than being deleted with the unused binding
a read through a Proxy still runs the trap even when the value goes nowhere
`delete`, `instanceof`, a tagged template and `new` all survive compression
the compressor reports `pure()` as false for every one of those shapes, so no pass can delete them
a directive-looking string with an escape in it is NOT a directive, and stays spelled exactly as written
a real prologue stays first and stays strict
a local binding named `undefined` keeps its meaning (the parameter shadows the global)
a hole in an array stays a hole
a nested hole in a destructuring pattern stays a hole
the tool requires nothing from outside itself and nothing but the node built-ins (16 require calls in 9 files)
no socket, no subprocess and no dynamic evaluation anywhere in the tool (the two mentions in scope.js are detections, not uses)
no package manifest was added: the tool has no dependencies to install and no build step to run
every file of the tool is valid JavaScript on its own (node --check on 9 files)
`fn.toString()` is NOT preserved: the printed text is what a caller gets (a documented non-guarantee, asserted rather than hidden)
with an output file the CLI writes the code and its map (a map is the default, as --help says) and nothing else
with --no-source-map exactly one file is written
the input file is not modified

scope: the negatives, measured by running code: eval/with/Function switch renaming off, text-in-strings blocks a name, fn.name and arity are untouched, property names and observable reads survive, directives and shadowed `undefined` keep their meaning, and the tool has no dependency, no socket and no subprocess. The one documented difference (fn.toString) is asserted as a difference.
